title: Push the nano-SIM out of a triple-cut SIM card, leaving the micro and mini frames in the card
instruction: Push the nano-SIM out of the card, leaving the micro and mini frames in the card.
context: New phone lines and replacement SIMs ship on triple-cut cards; carriers tell users to pop out the size they need by hand and keep the white frames as adapters. The parts nest: a 12.3 x 8.8 mm nano in a 1.5 mm micro ring in the mini outline. One hand holds the card so it can't tip, the other presses inside the nano only; a press on the ring or across a cut tears the frames out instead.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights above the table. Notebook stack (SimReady misc_notebook_a01/a02, fixed): four closed paper notebooks, each 22.9 x 17.0 x 1.0 cm, about 250 g, stacked 4.0 cm high, centred at (30, 8.5), right edge (the -y edge) at y = 0. SIM card: triple-cut (2FF/3FF/4FF) carrier card, ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1, 8.56 x 5.40 x 0.076 cm white PVC, 5 g, chip side up, lying flat on the stack with its long side along y, centred at (30.0, 0.8); its right end is 3.5 cm out over the stack's edge, the cut-outs at that end. Cut-outs, nested and concentric: mini (2FF) 2.5 x 1.5 cm, its outer edge 0.625 cm from the card's right end; micro (3FF) 1.5 x 1.2 cm; nano (4FF) 1.23 x 0.88 cm with gold contacts, centred at (29.7, -1.6). Distractors (SimReady, loose, not scored): ceramic mug dishware_mug_a01, 11.4 x 9.0 x 8.0 cm, 300 g, at (52, 22); eyeglasses accessory_eyeglasses_a01, 14.5 x 17.4 x 5.7 cm, 30 g, at (56, -16); plastic ballpoint pen stationery_pen_plastic_a01, 17.8 x 1.5 x 1.2 cm, 12 g, lying at (17, -20). Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read at the end (real trial: photos of the card's chip side and of the table, and the video). A part is torn if any of its tabs is broken (sim: its tabs gave way); torn stays torn. The nano is out once its tabs gave way and it dropped clear of the card, unless it fell off the table (its centre more than 1 cm below the table top). 1.0: the nano out and lying on the table or the notebooks (its centre at most 4.3 cm above the table, moving under 1 cm/s), neither the micro ring nor the mini frame torn, the card flat (tilt at most 10 degrees) and still (under 1 cm/s and 3 degrees/s), and every fingertip point of both grippers at least 3 cm from the card and from the nano, all held 1 s; it stays 1.0 while the nano is out and both frames are untorn. 0.75: the nano out and both frames untorn, without the 1.0 conditions. 0.5: the nano out, but the micro ring or the mini frame torn. 0.25: the nano not out, and the micro ring or the mini frame torn. 0: the nano not out and neither frame torn. Overriding all of these, 0 if the card was ever more than 2 cm below the table top (knocked off the table).
reset_notes: The card is consumed: a fresh triple-cut card (about US$8 each) for each trial, laid on its tape outline on the notebook stack. Pick up the nano and any frames.
fidelity: Card: rigid PVC plates (primitives) on sliders; each part's tabs are one stiff spring that gives way at a set load (nano 5, micro 7, mini 9 N: estimates). No bending. A torn-loose nano drags on its cut edges until clear (damping), then drops out of the underside on its slider, staying level. Tab sliders get extra joint inertia for solver stability. Notebooks fixed, with one 4 cm box collider for the stack. Notebooks, mug, glasses, pen: SimReady.
